title: Pump bearing overtemperature
text: Pump bearing temperature above the max limit usually means lubrication failure, contamination, or misalignment. Check oil level and condition, then shaft alignment. Do not run the pump to failure; shut down at critical levels.

title: Pump vibration and cavitation
text: High pump vibration with a gravel-like noise indicates cavitation. Check suction strainer, suction valve position and NPSH margin. Vibration with a once-per-rev peak points to imbalance or a bent shaft.

title: Pump mechanical seal leaks
text: A weeping mechanical seal leaks a few drops per minute and can be monitored. A steady stream means seal face damage: isolate the pump, check seal flush plan and shaft sleeve wear.

title: Motor bearing wear
text: Rising motor bearing temperature with increasing vibration suggests bearing wear or over-greasing. Check grease interval, grease type compatibility and shaft current (VFD fluting).

title: Motor overheating windings
text: Hot motor casing with normal bearing temperature points to winding or cooling problems. Check cooling fan, blocked vents, supply voltage imbalance and overload relay settings.

title: Motor and pump coupling misalignment
text: Axial vibration at twice running speed is a misalignment signature. Re-check coupling alignment with a laser tool and look for soft foot at the baseplate.

title: Compressor discharge temperature
text: High compressor bearing or discharge temperature: check cooler fouling, oil level, oil filter differential pressure and intake air filter. Repeated high-temp trips need a lube oil analysis.

title: Compressor vibration surge
text: Pulsing vibration with pressure swings can indicate surge or valve failure. Check suction and discharge valve plates, anti-surge controller state and unloader operation.

title: Compressor service interval
text: Reciprocating compressors have a 6 month service interval covering valves, rings and oil change. Overdue service raises the risk of valve failure and oil carryover.

title: Fan imbalance
text: Fan vibration at 1x running speed is typically imbalance from dirt build-up or blade damage. Inspect blades, clean, and re-balance. Check for cracked welds on the impeller.

title: Fan bearing lubrication
text: Fan bearings in dusty areas overheat when grease is contaminated. Purge and re-grease per schedule; verify seals are intact. Do not over-grease.

title: Fan belt drive
text: Squealing and uneven vibration on belt-driven fans suggests slipping or worn belts. Check belt tension and sheave wear; replace belts as a matched set.

title: Gearbox oil and temperature
text: Gearbox temperature rise with metallic debris on the magnetic plug indicates gear or bearing wear. Take an oil sample, check oil level and cooler, and plan inspection of gear teeth.

title: Gearbox vibration
text: High gear-mesh vibration with noise may mean tooth wear or backlash. Compare to baseline spectrum and inspect through the inspection cover at next shutdown.

title: General service interval policy
text: Equipment past its service interval must be scheduled for service. Overdue alone is not an emergency, but it raises the baseline risk of any other abnormal reading.

title: Safety limits are not adjustable in the field
text: Alarm and trip limits are set by engineering. A technician or operator may not raise, bypass or reinterpret a limit. Any limit change goes through management of change.

title: Escalation for unknown equipment
text: If the equipment tag cannot be matched to the asset register, confirm the tag on the nameplate before acting on readings, because limits depend on the equipment type.

title: Missing readings
text: When temperature or vibration readings are missing, take a fresh measurement with a calibrated instrument before deciding. Treat reports of smoke, burning smell or seizing as urgent regardless.
